science.title: From flower moon to blue moon, May brings several lunar events
science.description: Skywatchers in Moose Jaw and across Saskatchewan have several lunar events to watch this month, from the flower moon earlier in May to a rare blue micro moon later in the month. Astronomer Abigail Sadowski said May began with what is traditionally known as the flower moon, the name given to the full moon that occurs in May. “It has a slightly different name based on the month it happens in,” Sadowski said. She said names such as flower moon, harvest moon and strawberry moon do not describe the moon’s appearance, despite common misconceptions. “This doesn’t mean it looks any different from your standard full moon,” she said. She explained the “super” designation means the moon is at perigee, its closest point to Earth, during the new moon phase. While the moon itself will not be visible, the darker skies around a new moon can improve viewing conditions for stargazers. “It will be nice and dark, and you’ll hopefully be able to see some fainter objects if you have a telescope,” Sadowski said. She added that evenings following a new moon can also offer opportunities to spot earthshine, where sunlight reflected from Earth faintly illuminates the darker portion of the crescent moon. This month’s blue moon will also be a micro moon, meaning the moon will be at apogee, its farthest point from Earth, while full. “Being farther from Earth makes it look 14 per cent smaller than a supermoon and seven per cent smaller than a normal moon,” Sadowski said.
